question: Does a single-size GHZ optical-clock protocol enlarge normalized capability, or does its short-time precision gain remain absorbed by changed control and reduced dynamic range?

construction.retention_statement: The branch uses the completed Cao et al. experiment's own operational envelope: short-dark-time sub-SQL frequency instability together with the reported reduced dynamic range and no optimal-dark-time precision improvement over unentangled atoms.

branches.label: single-size GHZ clock interrogation
branches.normalization_frame: Compare achievable clock precision over the operational dark-time and dynamic-range envelope, while accounting for GHZ preparation and control. A short-time variance gain does not enlarge the normalized task set when the same protocol loses usable range and does not improve optimum precision.

assumptions: The completed Cao et al. experiment is used only for the claims stated in its abstract-level operational result.
Capability means an executable task-set change after the declared resource, access, and control normalization, not lower variance at one operating point.
The reduced dynamic range and optimal-dark-time comparison are part of the assessed object rather than omitted costs.
tests: validate the Transition Diagnosis v0.1 contract
require the capability overclaim to be rejected when normalized tasks remain equal
falsifiers: a matched full-envelope comparison establishes a previously impossible estimation decision task at the same atom, time, control, prior, readout, and error budgets
the reported dynamic-range loss is removed without adding a new control or resource
the classification changes under endpoint relabeling
nonclaims: No claim is made that entanglement lacks metrological value.
No raw precision number is converted into capability without a decision-task threshold and matched budget.
No capability, finality, universality, hierarchy, or source-verdict claim is established.
reopening_conditions: a source-backed full-envelope resource-normalized task comparison becomes available
a user supplies a decision threshold for which the short-time gain changes executability
the control or readout boundary is reformulated with an independently justified normalization
